summary: ethereum-vault-connector exfiltrates installer credentials to webhook.site on npm install
details: The package declares both preinstall and postinstall as `node index.js` in package.json, so index.js executes automatically on `npm install`. index.js reads installer-side secret files including ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, ~/.kube/config, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.netrc, ~/.npmrc, ~/.gitconfig, ~/.git-credentials, gcloud application default credentials, and Solana/Anchor/NEAR/Sui/Foundry keystores; scrapes environment variables matching /KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASS|PRIVATE|MNEMONIC|WALLET|SEED|AWS|GITHUB|NPM/; collects.env files from the current working directory; and gathers host metadata (os.hostname, os.userInfo().username, cwd, platform, arch). The bundle is POSTed via https.request to webhook.site/326b0891-2093-4800-a4c1-686ce3e07b09. The package name and description impersonate Euler Labs' Ethereum Vault Connector but ship no contract or library code — only the credential-stealing index.js — with a comment framing it as an 'install-time environment diagnostics shim'.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
